failureMessage: waitForFunction takes an async predicate's promise as truthy and resolves at once, on every engine, so the test passes only while the page happens to be fast
fix: wait with until(page, fn, arg) from web-tests/page_until.mjs, which polls the page until the async predicate resolves truthy

matchLines.what: waits on an async predicate with waitForFunction, which never waits: {match}

failureMessage: a test that sleeps a fixed time guesses how long the page takes: too short on a slow runner, so it flakes, and wasted on every fast one
fix: wait for what the next check reads (waitForFunction, waitForSelector, until()), have a stand-in hold its answer until the test releases it (held() from web-tests/held.mjs), or move the page's clock with ctx.clock; where only real time will do, end the line `// waits on purpose: <reason>`, and a deadline that only bounds a hang `// bounds a hang: <reason>`

matchLines.what: waits a fixed time instead of for what it needs: {match}

failureMessage: a frame wait copied into each driver drifts: one waits one frame, the next two, and nobody can say which a page needs
Google is a detail of the remote store and the identity provider, so code elsewhere that depends on it breaks when that detail changes
fix: move it into web/drive.js (behind `remote`) or web/account.js; an older browser key or cache path may stay, as a constant alone on its line

matchLines.what: names Google or Drive outside web/drive.js and web/account.js: {match}

failureMessage: a timer set anywhere in page code is a cadence nobody can list, a visual effect guessing how long it takes, or a poll running on in a hidden tab
fix: a visual effect is a CSS transition or animation, acted on at transitionend or animationend; background work goes through every(), settle(), within() or after() in web/pacing.js; where only a raw timer will do, end the line `// timed here: <reason>`
